result: {"C1": ["Prefers building or using simple code tools for black-box investigation over working only in the bare playground, because fiddly prompt-engineering work benefits from programmatic support.", "Prefers causal evidence from feature ablation or intervention over correlational observation of suspicious features, because flipping features on and off shows which ones are actually responsible."], "C2": ["Prefers deep hands-on interactive familiarity with model behavior over purely internals-based or abstract analysis, because good hypotheses about what to test and what to explain come from long interaction.", "Prefers reasoning about synthetic-input detection in Bayesian terms, because a given tell matters less as the prior that inputs are synthetic rises at scale."], "C3": ["Prefers calibrated, prior-aware interpretation of evidence over treating single observations as decisive, because one observation only shifts beliefs much if egregious misalignment was already plausible.", "Prefers treating single-setting results as modest evidence that supports transferable methodology rather than specific numbers or protocol rankings, because one setting rarely establishes general claims."], "C4": ["Prefers preparing AI control plans for plausibly scheming models over relying on evidence-triggered shutdown, because other developers may not undeploy even given strong evidence.", "Prefers balancing artifacts across labels over filtering artifact-bearing examples, because filtering creates new artifacts and removes legitimate phenomena."], "C5": ["Prefers distrusting bad behavior found through hard adversarial search as evidence of scheming, because models are not adversarially robust and non-schemers also produce bad or incoherent outputs.", "Prefers interpreting insensitivity to a manipulation by enumerating competing explanations and checking reasoning transcripts over settling on a single story, because several mechanisms can produce the same behavior."]}
